newsitem.title: UK: Poll set to seal fate of EMAP "dissidents".
newsitem.headline: Poll set to seal fate of EMAP "dissidents".

text.p: A poll of shareholders at UK media group EMAP Plc was set to confirm the removal of two rebel non-executive directors when the results were announced on Monday. An announcement is due around 1400 GMT.

Shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting, in a show of hands, voted more than three-to-one in favour of the removal of non-executives Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke, who have opposed recent changes to the company's articles.
Corporate governance lobby group PIRC called for a poll, under which votes are counted in proportion to shares held. EMAP said proxies received strongly backed the removal of the pair.
Deputy chairman Richard Winfrey said 108.8 million proxy votes had been registered in favour of the removal of the pair and only 11.1 million against.
Chairman Sir John Hoskyns told the EGM that the board regretted the acrimonious departure of Simmonds and Cooke.
"The board will do its best to ensure that the (EMAP) success story continues," he said.

Simmonds struck a conciliatory note after a bruising battle that has dragged on for several months and hit the company's share price. "Catharsis and thinking about the future are good things. EMAP is going to continue to be great," he said.
His fellow rebel Cooke had earlier said that Hoskyns should "stand down soonest". He also attacked chief executive Robin Miller for his part in the dispute.

The row centred around a change of articles approve by the company's Annual General Meeting in July. These removed a provision to retain at least five non-executive directors and also enabled a director to be ousted on a 75 percent board vote.
"I am confident that with these two resolutions passed, the board will be fully united and ready to give full attention to running your company's business," Hoskyns added.
Hoskyns, who intends to retire as chairman in 1998, said press reports that he had favoured Miller as his successor were not correct.
He also played down talk of a rift between Miller and managing director David Arculus.
"Robin and David have worked in partnership since 1974. That partnership has always been based on hard thinking, vigorous argument and mutual trust," he said.
